## Reviewer

### Summary

The paper studies the problem of Byzantine robust distributed learning and proposes an adaptive clipping scheme for the gradients before applying robust aggregation methods. The paper theoretically shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method and empirically shows that it can improve the robustness of the learning.

### Soundness

3 good

### Presentation

3 good

### Contribution

2 fair

### Strengths

The paper is well written and easy to follow. The proposed method is simple and intuitive and the theoretical analysis is sound. The experiments are well conducted and the results are promising.

### Weaknesses

The main weakness of the paper is that the theoretical analysis is not very strong. The paper shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method, but it does not provide any new robustness guarantees. The empirical results are promising, but it is not clear whether the proposed method is the best approach for Byzantine robust distributed learning.

### Questions

- The paper claims that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method, but it does not provide any new robustness guarantees. Can you provide more details on this claim?
- The paper does not compare the proposed method with other Byzantine robust distributed learning methods. Can you provide more details on how the proposed method compares to other methods?

### Flag For Ethics Review

No ethics review needed.

### Rating

6: marginally above the acceptance threshold

### Confidence

4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.

## Reviewer

### Summary

This paper proposes a new adaptive clipping scheme for distributed learning with Byzantine workers. The authors first show that the standard static clipping is not robust. Then they propose a new adaptive clipping scheme, termed Adaptive Robust Clipping (ARC), which dynamically adjusts the clipping threshold as per the gradients sent by the workers and the fraction of adversarial workers to be tolerated. The authors show that ARC preserves the robustness guarantee of the original robust aggregation method and improves the empirical performance of state-of-the-art Robust-DGD methods.

### Soundness

3 good

### Presentation

3 good

### Contribution

3 good

### Strengths

1. The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
2. The proposed adaptive clipping scheme is simple and effective.
3. The authors provide theoretical analysis and empirical results to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

### Weaknesses

1. The proposed adaptive clipping scheme is similar to the one proposed in Diakonikolas et al. (2020). The authors should discuss the differences between their proposed method and the one in Diakonikolas et al. (2020).
2. The authors should provide more details about the experimental settings, such as the hyperparameters used in the experiments.

### Questions

See Weaknesses.

No ethics review needed.

### Rating

6: marginally above the acceptance threshold

### Confidence

4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.

### Summary

The paper studies the problem of Byzantine robust distributed learning and proposes an adaptive clipping scheme for the gradients before applying robust aggregation methods. The paper theoretically shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method and empirically shows that it can improve the robustness of the learning.

### Soundness

3 good

3 good

### Strengths

The paper is well written and easy to follow. The proposed method is simple and intuitive and the theoretical analysis is sound. The experiments are well conducted and the results are promising.

### Weaknesses

The main weakness of the paper is that the theoretical analysis is not very strong. The paper shows that the proposed method preserves the robustness of the original aggregation method, but it does not provide any new robustness guarantees. The empirical results are promising, but it is not clear whether the proposed method is the best approach for Byzantine robust distributed learning.

## Reviewer

### Summary

This paper proposes a new adaptive clipping scheme for distributed learning with Byzantine workers. The authors first show that the standard static clipping is not robust. Then they propose a new adaptive clipping scheme, termed Adaptive Robust Clipping (ARC), which dynamically adjusts the clipping threshold as per the gradients sent by the workers and the fraction of adversarial workers to be tolerated. The authors show that ARC preserves the robustness guarantee of the original robust aggregation method and improves the empirical performance of state-of-the-art Robust-DGD methods.

### Soundness

3 good

### Presentation

3 good

### Contribution

### Weaknesses
